title: Verdi's opera
subject: art
description: Giuseppe Verdi made Italian opera a political weapon and a theater of the soul: Rigoletto, Traviata, Aida, Otello.

hero.hook: From slave choirs to tricolor flags: when opera unifies Italy.

blocks.text: **Giuseppe Verdi** (**1813**-**1901**) is not only the greatest Italian opera composer of the 19th century. He is the musical voice of Italian unity and the renovator of a genre that he leads towards a new psychological realism.

From *Rigoletto* to *La Traviata*, his works leave the living room to talk about politics, honor, love and injustice. Facing the German **Richard Wagner**, Verdi remains faithful to Italian melodic clarity, but densifies the drama.

sections.title: Before Verdi: bel canto and the drama revolution

blocks.text: The **opera**, born in Florence around **1600**, was the great European entertainment in the 19th century. At the beginning of the century, [[Bel canto]] reigned: vocal virtuosity, beautiful melodies. **Rossini** and **Donizetti** dominate.

Verdi admires these masters, but considers their librettos too artificial. For him, music must serve the drama: each note conveys an urgency or a feeling. He adapts **Shakespeare**, **Victor Hugo**, and densifies the orchestra. While Wagner dreams of a total mythological work, Verdi anchors the opera in the social reality of his time.
In 1832, the Milan Conservatory refused Verdi: examiners judged his hand position on the piano “defective” and his talent insufficient.

In **1842**, *Nabucco* triumphs. The opera tells of the exile of the Hebrews to Babylon. In an Italy occupied by the Austrian Empire, the slave choir *Go, think* became a clandestine anthem. Verdi became a figure of [[The Italian Risorgimento]], the national unification movement.

blocks.caption: Va, pensiero: an opera chorus turned patriotic anthem.

blocks.text: In the 1850s, “Viva VERDI” was written on the walls. Behind the name hides the acronym: **Vittorio Emanuele Re D'Italia**. Verdi, supporter of the cause, was elected deputy in **1861** under the aegis of [[Cavour]], architect of unity. His operas feature marginalized people facing order: the jester of *Rigoletto*, the struggles of *Trouvère*.
In Venice, patriotic spectators threw bouquets of green, white and red onto the stage to form the banned Italian flag.

sections.title: Rigoletto, Traviata, Aida: realism on stage

blocks.text: The “popular trilogy” sets a new standard: *Rigoletto* (**1851**), *Il Trovatore* and *La Traviata* (**1853**). Gone are the only ancient kings: Rigoletto is a hunchbacked jester, far from the hero of [[Opera seria vs. opera buffa]].

*La Traviata*, after *The Lady of the Camellias* by **Alexandre Dumas son**, shocks: a contemporary Parisian courtesan dies of tuberculosis. The censorship wants to push the action back into the past. Verdi holds on. In **1871**, *Aida*, commissioned for Cairo and the Suez Canal, mixes spectacle and conflict between love and duty.

blocks.caption: La Traviata: the scandal of an opera too modern for its time.

blocks.text: For *Aida*, Verdi had straight “Theban trumpets” made, inspired by ancient Egyptian bas-reliefs.

After 70 years, pushed by the publisher Ricordi and the librettist **Arrigo Boito**, Verdi returns with *Otello* (**1887**) and *Falstaff* (**1893**). It abandons the classic alternation between [[Recitative]] and arias for fluid dramatic continuity. *Falstaff*, composed at age 79, concludes: “Everything in the world is a joke.”

When he died in **1901**, more than **300,000** people followed the funeral in Milan and sang *Nabucco*. He bequeathed his fortune to a retirement home for musicians. His influence nourishes Italian [[Verismo]] and all modern musical theater.

events.title: Nabucco
events.detail: Va, pensiero becomes anthem of the Risorgimento.

blocks.text: Verdi transformed Italian opera into political and human theater: from the chorus of Risorgimento to the realism of Traviata, to Falstaff.
